title.narrative: Private Sector Jobs and Economic Transformation (PSJET)

description.narrative: Contribute to labor demand by supporting MSMEs and value chains resilience and growth through improved business development services and access to financial resources

The project still focuses on reducing fragility by contributing to labor demand by strengthening MSMEs and value chains resilience to crises and their expansion through business development services and access to capital. This goal will be achieved by improving the capacity of firms to adjust to the new market conditions brought by crises and by increasing the capacity of the financial sector to mitigate risks when lending to MSMEs (including new young entrepreneurs and self-employed ones) in an uncertain economic environment. The development of Haiti has suffered from high political, economic, social, and climate-related risks. Evidence suggests that job opportunities can reduce individual motivations to engage in violence and destabilizing activities, and that greater well-being is linked with less conflict and violence. The job environment in Haiti suffers from limited growth of firms in a context of difficult business environment; significant constraints on financial resources to support recovery; socio-political instability; disaster and climate related risks; and violence and insecurity. The project is being adjusted to respond to the Haiti Rapid Crisis Impact Assessment (RCIA) conducted between July and October 2024 under the leadership of the Ministry of Economy and Finance with the support of the World Bank, United Nations, European Union, and Inter-American Development Bank. The project still includes key elements for job creation and firm growth; increasing firm productivity through upgrading capabilities; improving access to markets; and improving access to finance.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2 Section I A 1 to 8 (Institutional Arrangements)1. The Recipient shall vest the overall responsibility for theimplementation of the Project in MEF through the DEE and the PCU and ensure that: (a) Parts 1 and 3 are carried out or caused to becarried out by MEF and MCI; (b) Part 2 is caused to be carried out by FDI; and (c) Part 4 of the Project is carried out or causedto be carried out through one or more implementing agencies or entities, as shall be further defined in the CER Manual; all inaccordance with the Operational Manual, the Subsidiary Agreement, the On-Lending Manual and the Sub-grant Manual (when adopted) andthe ESCP, as applicable.2. The Recipient shall operate and maintain, at all times during the implementation of the Project, theDEE under the administrative authority of MEF, and assign to the DEE functions, staffing and resources satisfactory to theAssociation, as further detailed in the Operational Manual.3. The Recipient shall ensure that the DEE shall be responsible foroverall planning, coordination and technical monitoring of Project activities, joint preparation of the Annual Work Plans,monitoring of progress reports, communication on Project activities as further detailed in the Operational Manual.4. The Recipientshall operate and maintain, at all times during the implementation of the Project, the PCU under the administrative authority ofMEF, with functions, staffing and resources satisfactory to the Association, as further detailed in the Operational Manual.5 TheRecipient shall ensure that the PCU shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration, fiduciary aspects (procurement,disbursement, environmental and social safeguards, and financial management), joint preparation of the Annual Work Plans,monitoring, evaluation, reporting on Project activities; as further detailed in the Operational Manual.6. The Recipient shalloperate and maintain, at all times during the implementation of the Project, the Project Strategic Committee and the ProjectTechnical Committee under the leadership of MEF through the DEE, with functions, composition and resources satisfactory to theAssociation, as further detailed in the Operational Manual.7 The Recipient shall ensure that the Project Strategic Committeeconvenes at least twice per year to review Project progress in implementing Annual Work Plans prepared by the DEE and the PCU andto advise on performance targets and timelines for proposed activities under the Project; as further detailed in the OperationalManual.8. The Recipient shall ensure that the Project Technical Committee convenes at least every month to ensure coordination ofthe Project and address bottlenecks in the implementation of the Project, as further detailed in the Operational Manual.

Schedule 2 Section I B 1 and 2 (Operational Manual)1. The Recipient shall adopt not later than one month after the Effective Dateand thereafter carry out the Project in accordance with a manual (the Operational Manual), satisfactory in form and substance tothe Association, which consists of different schedules setting forth rules, methods, guidelines, specific development plans,standard documents, and procedures for the carrying out of the Project, including, inter alia, the following:(a) the detaileddescription of all Project activities, their sequencing and the prospective timetable, budget and steps in relationthereto;(b) the Project administrative, financial, accounting, safeguards, auditing, procurement, and disbursement procedures,including all relevant standard documents;(c) the monitoring indicators for the Project; and(d) the grievance mechanisms andthe code of ethics and conduct.2. The Operational Manual may be amended from time to time in consultation with, and afterapproval of, the Association. In case of any conflict between the terms of the Operational Manual and those of this Agreement, theterms of this Agreement shall prevail.

Schedule 2 Section I C 1 and 2 (On-Lending Manual)1. The Recipient shall cause FDI and the PFIs to carry out Parts 2.1 and 2.3 ofthe Project in accordance with a manual (the On-Lending Manual), satisfactory in form and substance to the Association, whichconsists of different schedules setting forth rules, methods, guidelines, specific development plans, standard documents, andprocedures for the carrying out of Parts 2.1 and 2.3 of the Project, including the following:(a) the detailed description of allactivities under Parts 2.1 and 2.3 of the Project, their sequencing and the prospective timetable, budget and benchmarks inrelation thereto;(b) the eligibility criteria for MSMEs, the negative list of activities, the model form for the Sub-loanAgreements, including the criteria and procedures to be met by MSMEs to receive such Sub-loans;(c) the Project administrative,financial, accounting, auditing, procurement, and disbursement procedures, including all relevant standard documents, as well asthe criteria for the selection of MSMEs;(d) environmental and social management arrangements and instruments adopted inaccordance with the Environmental and Social Standards of Section I.H of this Schedule 2;(e) the monitoring indicators for Parts2.1 and 2.3 of the Project; and(f) the grievance mechanisms and the code of ethics and conduct.2. The On-Lending Manual may beamended from time to time in consultation with, and after approval of, the Association. In case of any conflict between the termsof the On-Lending Manual and those of this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall prevail.

Schedule 2 Section I D 1 and 2 (Sub-grant Manual)1. The Recipient shall carry out Parts 1.1 (ii) and 1.2(ii) of the Project inaccordance with a manual (the Sub-grant Manual), satisfactory in form and substance to the Association, which consists of differentschedules setting forth rules, methods, guidelines, specific development plans, standard documents, and procedures for the carryingout of Parts 1.1(ii) and 1.2(ii) of the Project, including the following:(a) the detailed description of all activities underPart 1.1(ii) and 1.2(ii) of the Project, their sequencing and the prospective timetable, budget and benchmarks in relationthereto;(b) the eligibility criteria for Beneficiary Firms, the negative list, the model form for the Sub-grant Agreements,including the criteria and procedures to be met by Beneficiary Firms to receive such Sub-grants;(c) the Project administrative,financial, accounting, auditing, procurement, and disbursement procedures, including all relevant standard documents; as well asthe criteria for the selection of Beneficiary Firms;(d) the environmental and social management arrangements and instrumentsadopted in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards of Section I.H of this Schedule 2;(e) the monitoring indicatorsfor Parts 1.1(ii) and 1.2(ii) of the Project; and(f) the grievance mechanisms and the code of ethics and conduct.2. TheSub-grant Manual may be amended from time to time in consultation with, and after approval of, the Association. In case of anyconflict between the terms of the Sub-grant Manual and those of this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall prevail.

Schedule 2 Section I E 1, 2 and 3 (Annual Work Plans)1. Without limitation to the obligations set forth in Section I.B above, theRecipient shall carry out the Project in accordance with Annual Work Plans to be prepared and furnished to the Association notlater than October 31 of each calendar year during the implementation of the Project (the first such Annual Work Plan being due onemonth after the Effective Date), and containing all activities proposed for inclusion in the Project for the next calendar year,including: (a) detailed timetables for the sequencing and implementation of proposed Project activities; (b) types of expendituresrequired for such activities and a proposed financing plan and sources of funding for such expenditures; and (c) any OperatingCosts or Training that may be required under the Project.2. The Recipient shall afford the Association a reasonable opportunity toexchange views on each such proposed Annual Work Plan; and, thereafter ensure that the Project is implemented with due diligenceduring said following calendar year in accordance with such Annual Work Plan as shall have been approved by the Association.3. TheAnnual Work Plans may only be amended from time to time in consultation with, and after approval of, the Association. In case ofany conflict between the terms of the Annual Work Plans and those of this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall prevail.

Schedule 2 Section I F 1, 2 and 3 (Contingent Emergency Response) 1. In order to ensure the proper implementation of contingentemergency response activities under Part 4 of the Project (“Emergency Response Part”), the Recipient shall:(a) prepare and furnishto the Association for its review and approval, a Contingency Emergency Response Manual (“CER Manual”) which shall set forthdetailed implementation arrangements for the Emergency Response Part, including: (i) any additional institutional structures orarrangements for coordinating and implementing the Emergency Response Part; (ii) specific activities which may be included in theEmergency Response Part, Eligible Expenditures required therefor (“Emergency Expenditures”), and any procedures for such inclusion;(iii) financial management arrangements for the Emergency Response Part; (iv) procurement methods and procedures for the EmergencyResponse Part; (v) documentation required for withdrawals of Emergency Expenditures; (vi) environmental and social managementarrangements and instruments for the Emergency Response Part adopted in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards ofSection I.H of this Schedule 2; and (vii) any other arrangements necessary to ensure proper coordination and implementation of theEmergency Response Part;(b) afford the Association a reasonable opportunity to review the proposed CER Manual;(c) promptly adoptthe CER Manual for the Emergency Response Part as shall have been approved by the Association and integrate it as an annex to theOperational Manual;(d) ensure that the Emergency Response Part is carried out in accordance with the CER Manual; provided,however, that in the event of any inconsistency between the provisions of the CER Manual and this Agreement, the provisions of thisAgreement shall prevail; and(e) not amend, suspend, abrogate, repeal or waive any provision of the CER Manual without the priorwritten approval by the Association.2. The Recipient shall, throughout the implementation of the Emergency Response Part, maintainthe institutional structures and arrangements established in accordance with the CER Manual, with adequate staff and resourcessatisfactory to the Association.3. The Recipient shall undertake no activities under the Emergency Response Part unless and untilthe following conditions have been met in respect of said activities:(a) the Recipient has determined that an Eligible Crisis orEmergency has occurred, has furnished to the Association a request to include said activities in the Emergency Response Part inorder to respond to said Eligible Crisis or Emergency, and the Association has agreed with such determination, accepted saidrequest and notified the Recipient thereof; and (b) the Recipient has ensured the preparation and disclosure of all environmentaland social instruments as may be required for said activities in accordance with the CER Manual, the Association has approved allsaid instruments, and the Recipient has ensured the implementation of any actions which are required to be taken under saidinstruments.

Schedule 2 Section I G 1 and 2 (Subsidiary Agreement)1. To facilitate the carrying out of Part 2 of the Project, the Recipientshall make part of the proceeds of the Financing allocated to Categories (3) and (4) available to FDI under a subsidiary agreement(the “Subsidiary Agreement”) to be entered into between the Recipient and FDI, under terms and conditions approved by theAssociation, which shall include the following:(a) the right of the Recipient, to take remedial actions against the FDI, in casethe FDI shall have failed to comply with any of its obligations under the Subsidiary Agreement, which actions may include, interalia, the partial or total suspension and/or cancellation or refund of all or any part of the proceeds of the Financing transferredto the FDI pursuant to the Subsidiary Agreement (as the case may be);(b) the obligation of the FDI to carry out Part 2 of theProject in collaboration with the International Fund Manager with due diligence and efficiency, in conformity with appropriateadministrative, economic, managerial, financial, environmental, social, and technical standards and practices, and provide promptlyas needed, the facilities, services and other resources required for Part 2 of the Project;(c) the obligation of the FDI toexchange views with the Recipient, and the Association with regard to the progress of Part 2 of the Project, and the performance ofits obligations under the Subsidiary Agreement;(d) the obligation of the FDI to promptly inform the Recipient and the Associationof any condition which interferes or threatens to interfere with the progress of Part 2 of the Project;(e) the obligation of theFDI to: (i) carry out Part 2 of the Project in accordance with the Operational Manual, the On-Lending Manual, the Anti-CorruptionGuidelines and the provisions set forth in Section I.H of this Schedule; and (ii) take or permit to be taken all actions in orderto enable the Recipient to comply with its obligations under this Agreement in respect of Part 2 of the Project; and (f) theobligation of the FDI to: (i) maintain a financial management system and prepare financial statements in accordance withconsistently applied accounting standards acceptable to the Association, both in a manner adequate to reflect the operations,resources and expenditures related to Part 2 of the Project; and (ii) at the Association's or the Recipient's request, have suchfinancial statements audited by independent auditors acceptable to the Association, in accordance with consistently appliedauditing standards acceptable to the Association, and promptly furnish the statements as so audited to the Recipient and theAssociation.2. The Recipient shall exercise its rights and carry out its obligations under the Subsidiary Agreement in such amanner as to protect the interests of the Recipient and the Association in order to accomplish the purposes of the Financing.Except as the Association shall otherwise agree, the Recipient shall not amend, assign, abrogate, suspend, terminate, waive, orfail to enforce the Subsidiary Agreement or any of its provisions.

Schedule 2 Section I H 1- 6 (Environmental and Social Standards)1. The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is carried out inaccordance with the Environmental and Social Standards, in a manner acceptable to the Association.2. Without limitation uponparagraph 1 above, the Recipient shall ensure that the Project is implemented in accordance with the Environmental and SocialCommitment Plan (“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Association. To this end, the Recipient shall ensure that: (a) themeasures and actions specified in the ESCP are implemented with due diligence and efficiency, and provided in theESCP;(b) sufficient funds are available to cover the costs of implementing the ESCP;(c) policies and procedures are maintained,and qualified and experienced staff in adequate numbers are retained to implement the ESCP, as provided in the ESCP; and(d) theESCP, or any provision thereof, is not amended, repealed, suspended or waived, except as the Association shall otherwise agree inwriting, as specified in the ESCP, and ensure that the revised ESCP is disclosed promptly thereafter.3. In case of anyinconsistencies between the ESCP and the provisions of this Agreement, the provisions of this Agreement shall prevail. 4. TheRecipient shall ensure that:(a) all measures necessary are taken to collect, compile, and furnish to the Association throughregular reports, with the frequency specified in the ESCP, and promptly in a separate report or reports, if so requested by theAssociation, information on the status of compliance with the ESCP and the environmental and social instruments referred totherein, all such reports in form and substance acceptable to the Association, setting out, inter alia: (i) the status ofimplementation of the ESCP; (ii) conditions, if any, which interfere or threaten to interfere with the implementation of the ESCP;and (iii) corrective and preventive measures taken or required to be taken to address such conditions; and(b) the Association ispromptly notified of any incident or accident related to or having an impact on the Project which has, or is likely to have, asignificant adverse effect on the environment, the affected communities, the public or workers, in accordance with the ESCP, theenvironmental and social instruments referenced therein and the Environmental and Social Standards.5. The Recipient shallestablish, publicize, maintain and operate an accessible grievance mechanism, to receive and facilitate resolution of concerns andgrievances of Project-affected people, and take all measures necessary and appropriate to resolve, or facilitate the resolution of,such concerns and grievances, in a manner acceptable to the Association.6. The Recipient shall ensure that all bidding documentsand contracts for civil works under the Project include the obligation of contractors, and subcontractors to: (a) comply with therelevant aspects of ESCP and the environmental and social instruments referred to therein; and (b) adopt and enforce codes ofconduct that should be provided to and signed by all workers, detailing measures to address environmental, social, health andsafety risks, and the risks of sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and violence against children, all as applicable tosuch civil works commissioned or carried out pursuant to said contracts.

Schedule 2 Section I I 1- 3 (International Fund Manager)1. To facilitate the implementation and co-management of Parts 2.1 and2.3 of the Project, the Recipient shall hire with FDI, not later than twelve months after the Effective Date, under terms ofreference and in form and substance satisfactory to the Association through a Management Agreement, the International Fund Manager,and thereafter maintain said International Fund Manager during the implementation of the Project with functions, staffing andresources satisfactory to the Association, as further detailed in the Operational Manual and in the On Lending Manual.2. Withoutlimitation to the provisions of Sections I.A.1 of this Schedule, the Recipient shall ensure that Parts 2.1 and 2.3 are co-managedby the International Fund Manager and FDI; as further detailed in the On-Lending Manual. 3. The Recipient shall exercise itsrights (and cause FDI to exercise its rights) and carry out its obligations (and cause FDI to carry out its obligations) under theManagement Agreement in such a manner as to protect its interests, the interests of the FDI and the interests of the Association inorder to accomplish the purposes of the Financing. Except as the Association shall otherwise agree, the Recipient shall cause FDInot to amend, assign, abrogate, suspend, terminate, waive or fail to enforce the Management Agreement or any of its provisions.

Schedule 2 Section I J 1- 3 (MDODs)1. To facilitate the implementation of Parts 1 and 3.2 of the Project, the Recipient shall, nolater than six months after the Effective Date, hire one or several MDODs under terms of reference and in form and substancesatisfactory to the Association through one or several contracts (MDOD Contracts), and thereafter operate and maintain, said MDODswith functions, staffing and resources satisfactory to the Association, as further detailed in the Operational Manual andSub-grants Manual. 2. Without limitation to the provisions of Section I.A.1 of this Schedule, the Recipient shall ensure that theMDODs shall assist the DEE, the CFI and the MCI in the carrying out of Parts 1 and 3.2 of the Project, as further detailed in theOperational Manual and Sub-grants Manual. 3. The Recipient, through the DEE, the CFI and the MCI, shall exercise its rights andcarry out its obligations under the MDOD Contracts in such a manner as to protect the interests of the Recipient and theAssociation in order to accomplish the purposes of the Financing. Except as the Association shall otherwise agree, the Recipient,through the DEE, the CFI and the MCI, shall not amend, assign, abrogate, suspend, terminate, waive or fail to enforce the MDODContracts or any of their provisions.

Schedule 2 Section I K 1 and 2 (Sub-grants)1. To facilitate the carrying out of Part 1.1(ii) and Part 1.2 (ii) of the Project,the Recipient shall make the proceeds of the Financing allocated to Category (2) available to selected eligible Beneficiary Firmsunder an agreement (“Sub-grant Agreement”) to be entered into between the Recipient (through the MDOD) and said Beneficiary Firms,under terms and conditions approved by the Association and in accordance with the Sub-grant Manual. 2. The Recipient shall causethe MDOD to exercise its rights and carry out its obligations under the Sub-grant Agreements in such a manner as to protect theinterests of the Recipient and the Association in order to accomplish the purposes of the Financing. Except as the Associationshall otherwise agree, the Recipient shall cause the MDOD not to amend, assign, abrogate, suspend, terminate, waive or fail toenforce the Sub-grant Agreements or any of their provisions.

Schedule 2 Section I L 1 and 2 (Participation Agreements)1. To facilitate the carrying out of Part 2.1 of the Project, theRecipient shall cause FDI to make the proceeds of the Financing allocated to Category (4) available to selected PFIs under anagreement (“Participation Agreement”) to be entered into between the FDI and the selected PFIs, under terms and conditions approvedby the Association and in accordance with the On-Lending Manual. 2. The Recipient shall cause FDI to exercise its rights andcarry out its obligations under the Participation Agreements in such a manner as to protect the interests of the Recipient and theAssociation in order to accomplish the purposes of the Financing. Except as the Association shall otherwise agree, the Recipientshall cause FDI not to amend, assign, abrogate, suspend, terminate, waive or fail to enforce the Participation Agreements or any oftheir provisions.

Schedule 2 Section I M 1 and 2 (Sub-loans)1. To facilitate the carrying out of Part 2.1 of the Project, the Recipient shall causeFDI to make the proceeds of the Financing allocated to Category (4) available to PFIs to benefit selected MSMEs under an agreement(“Sub-loan Agreement”) to be entered into between the PFIs and selected MSMEs, under terms and conditions approved by theAssociation and in accordance with the On-Lending Manual.2. The Recipient, through FDI, shall cause the PFIs to exercise theirrights and carry out their obligations under the Sub-loan Agreements in such a manner as to protect the interests of the Recipientand the Association in order to accomplish the purposes of the Financing. Except as the Association shall otherwise agree, theRecipient, through FDI, shall cause the PFIs not to amend, assign, abrogate, suspend, terminate, waive or fail to enforce theSub-loan Agreements or any of their provisions.

Schedule 2 Section I N 1 and 2 (MSME Fund)1. To facilitate the carrying out of Part 2.3 of the Project, the Recipient shall notlater than six months prior to the Closing Date, request that the proceeds of the Financing allocated to Category (5) (if any) bemade available to FDI as an endowment to the MSME Fund, under terms and conditions approved by the Association and in accordancewith the Subsidiary Agreement, the Operational Manual and the On-Lending Manual. 2. The Recipient shall cause FDI to present areport on the activities of the MSME Fund on or prior to the Closing Date, in form and substance satisfactory to the Associationand in accordance with the format and content established in the On Lending Manual.
